title: Skeleton loading screens
when: The user wants grey shapes that show the layout of content while it loads, instead of a spinner.
inputs: the layout being loaded (cards, list, profile)
prompt:
Goal: Skeleton shapes that match the final layout, are hidden from screen readers and swap to content without layout shift.
Steps:
1. Build skeleton blocks with the same sizes as the real content: same image aspect-ratio, line heights and gaps.
2. Mark the skeleton container aria-hidden="true" and put a visually hidden Loading articles in a role="status" region.
3. Set aria-busy="true" on the content region while loading.
4. Shimmer: a linear-gradient with background-size: 200% 100% animating background-position; static under prefers-reduced-motion.
5. When data arrives, build the real nodes with createElement, replace the skeleton, clear aria-busy and update the status.
6. Show skeletons only when loading lasts over 300 ms.
Quality bar:
- No jump between skeleton and content.
- Skeleton colors come from tokens and work in dark mode.
- Three to six repeated items, not a whole page.
Pitfalls:
- Skeletons that never go away on errors.
- Screen readers reading empty boxes.
- Shapes unrelated to the final layout.
Verify:
- [ ] Skeletons are aria-hidden.
- [ ] A status region says what is loading.
- [ ] Reduced motion stops the shimmer.
- [ ] Content renders with textContent.
Output: Skeleton markup, skeleton.css and the swap logic in the page script.

examples.input: skeleton enquanto carrega os cards de produtos
examples.output: six grey card shapes with image and two lines, shimmer off with reduced motion, swapped for real cards with no shift
